hero.title: Which Oceania Cruise Ship Should You Choose?
hero.subtitle: A Complete Fleet Comparison Across Allura, Vista, Marina, Riviera, Nautica, Insignia & Sirena
hero.description: Choosing the right Oceania Cruises ship depends on the kind of vacation you want. Some travelers prefer newer ships with contemporary accommodations and a wider range of onboard spaces. Others enjoy smaller vessels that create a more intimate atmosphere and offer access to destination-focused boutique ports. Compare ship sizes, dining venues, and accommodations to find your ideal vessel.

fleetClasses.title: Oceania Cruises Fleet Overview & Classes
fleetClasses.subtitle: The current seven ships fall into three distinct architectural and experiential classes

items.title: Allura Class (Allura & Vista)
items.description: Debuted in 2023 and 2025, these 1,200-guest sister ships represent Oceania's latest evolution. They feature all-veranda staterooms, residential interior design, soaring Grand Lounges, and modern dining concepts like Aquamar Kitchen and The Bakery at Baristas.
features: Venues: Aquamar Kitchen, Ember, The Bakery at Baristas
Design: Contemporary residential luxury and expansive suites
Atmosphere: Balanced blend of boutique intimacy and modern amenities

items.title: O-Class (Marina & Riviera)
items.description: Carrying 1,250 guests, Marina and Riviera are celebrated as the culinary flagships of the fleet. Built with food lovers in mind, they feature multiple open-seating gourmet restaurants, custom Lalique glass staircases, and hands-on cooking demonstration centers.
features: Venues: Polo Grill, Toscana, Red Ginger, Jacques, Privée
Specialty: Hands-on Culinary Center and La Reserve wine pairings
Atmosphere: Sophisticated country-club casual with expansive public rooms

items.title: R-Class (Nautica, Insignia & Sirena)
items.description: Carrying just 670 guests, Oceania's smaller R-class vessels deliver the pinnacle of intimate cruising. Their compact size allows them to navigate narrow rivers, shallow coastal fjords, and historic city centers inaccessible to larger liners.
features: Venues: Four open-seating restaurants including Tuscan Steak on Sirena
Ports: Access to shallow boutique harbors and exotic World Cruise stops
Atmosphere: Classic traditional cruising with personalized, uncrowded service

ships.name: Oceania Allura
ships.bestFor: Newer ship design and all-veranda accommodations
ships.description: Oceania Allura entered service in 2025 and reflects Oceania's newest approach to residential-style design, culinary experiences, and personalized service. With all-veranda accommodations, wellness dining, and an expanded mixology program, she offers an ideal balance of intimacy and modern amenities.

ships.name: Oceania Vista
ships.bestFor: Aquamar Kitchen & The Bakery at Baristas
ships.description: Debuting in 2023, Vista introduced distinctive concepts like Aquamar Kitchen for wellness cuisine, The Bakery at Baristas for fresh French and Italian pastries, and dedicated solo veranda accommodations. Perfect for travelers seeking a vibrant, contemporary luxury aesthetic.

ships.name: Oceania Marina
ships.description: Designed with culinary enthusiasts in mind, Marina features multiple open-seating specialty restaurants, La Reserve by Wine Spectator for seven-course pairing dinners, Privée for private dining, and a custom Lalique crystal staircase in the grand atrium.

ships.name: Oceania Riviera
ships.description: Sister ship to Marina, Riviera carries approximately 1,250 guests and shares her culinary heritage. Known for its sophisticated residential decor, high-end art collection, and relaxed onboard atmosphere, Riviera delivers classic Oceania elegance on popular Mediterranean and Caribbean routes.

ships.name: Oceania Nautica
ships.description: Carrying just 670 guests, Nautica offers an intimate atmosphere with four open-seating gourmet restaurants, warm teak decks, and access to shallow harbor ports. Note: Nautica is scheduled to transform into Oceania Aurelia in November 2027 for extended global voyages.

ships.name: Oceania Insignia
ships.description: Insignia has undergone significant interior enhancements, featuring refreshed staterooms, updated marble bathrooms, and elegant public areas. As the flagship for Oceania's famed 180-day World Cruises, she offers a timeless small-ship atmosphere.

ships.name: Oceania Sirena
ships.description: Sirena combines intimate 670-guest cruising with distinctive dining, headlined by Tuscan Steak—a venue fusing Italian favorites with prime steaks and seafood—alongside Red Ginger and eight intimate lounges and bars.

decisionFactors.title: Six Things to Consider Before Choosing an Oceania Ship
decisionFactors.subtitle: Key factors that should guide your ship selection

items.title: Itinerary and Destinations
items.description: Always prioritize the ports of call, overnight dockings, and port times over ship age. A boutique R-class ship might visit remote Greek or Norwegian harbors that larger ships cannot enter.

items.title: Ship Size & Onboard Scale
items.description: Decide whether you prefer the 670-guest intimacy of R-class ships (Nautica, Insignia, Sirena) or the 1,200–1,250-guest scale of Allura, Vista, Marina, and Riviera with wider entertainment.

items.title: Dining Venue Preferences
items.description: Review restaurant menus before booking. Jacques (French) is only on Marina and Riviera; Tuscan Steak is exclusive to Sirena; Aquamar Kitchen and The Bakery are on Allura and Vista.

items.title: Accommodation Configurations
items.description: Allura and Vista are all-veranda ships. Marina, Riviera, and R-class ships offer inside and oceanview categories, allowing budget-conscious travelers to experience Oceania for less.

items.title: Onboard Amenities & Classes
items.description: If hands-on cooking classes are essential, choose Marina, Riviera, Vista, or Allura for their Culinary Centers. R-class ships have smaller spa and fitness footprints.

items.title: Total Real-World Vacation Budget
items.description: Compare complete fares including flights, transfers, and excursions. Promotional offers like Your World Included® apply fleetwide, but starting fares vary significantly by vessel and route.

finalRecommendations.title: Which Oceania Ship Should You Choose? Final Verdict
paragraphs: If your priority is the newest ship experience with contemporary residential decor and all-veranda staterooms, choose Oceania Allura (2025) or Oceania Vista (2023). They represent the pinnacle of modern luxury shipboard design.

If culinary depth and expansive public spaces are paramount, choose Oceania Marina or Oceania Riviera. Their Culinary Centers, La Reserve wine pairings, and Jacques Pépin French bistros remain the gold standard in premium gastronomy.

If you favor smaller ships with an unhurried, intimate atmosphere and access to boutique, shallow-water harbors worldwide, choose Oceania Nautica, Insignia, or Sirena. And for future global circumnavigations, keep an eye on Oceania Aurelia and Oceania Sonata arriving in 2027.

expert.bio: Having evaluated ships across every luxury brand, I find Oceania's fleet one of the most thoughtfully differentiated in cruising. Whether you choose the spacious modern grandeur of Vista and Allura, the culinary authority of Marina and Riviera, or the boutique intimacy of the R-class ships, you receive the same impeccable service and The Finest Cuisine at Sea®.
expert.quote: There is no wrong Oceania ship—only the right ship for your specific itinerary and travel style. If you want cutting-edge design, book Vista or Allura; if you want intimate port immersion, choose the smaller R-class.

faqs.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Oceania Cruises Ships
faqs.subtitle: Answers to the 20 most common questions travelers ask when choosing an Oceania vessel

questions.question: How many ships does Oceania Cruises have?
questions.answer: As of November 2026, Oceania Cruises operates seven ships: Allura, Vista, Marina, Riviera, Nautica, Insignia, and Sirena. Future ships scheduled for 2027 include Oceania Sonata and Oceania Aurelia.

questions.question: Which Oceania cruise ship is the best?
questions.answer: There is no single best ship for everyone. Allura and Vista are best for newer design and all-veranda staterooms; Marina and Riviera are best for culinary diversity and wine pairings; Nautica, Insignia, and Sirena are best for small-ship intimacy.

questions.question: What is the newest Oceania cruise ship?
questions.answer: Oceania Allura entered service in 2025, making it the newest operating ship in the fleet. Oceania Sonata is scheduled to debut as the flagship of the Sonata Class in August 2027.

questions.question: What is the largest Oceania cruise ship?
questions.answer: Currently, Marina and Riviera are the largest ships with a double-occupancy capacity of approximately 1,250 guests. The upcoming Oceania Sonata (August 2027) will accommodate approximately 1,390 guests.

questions.question: What is the smallest Oceania cruise ship?
questions.answer: Nautica, Insignia, and Sirena are the smallest ships, each carrying approximately 670 guests at double occupancy. Their compact size enables access to historic city centers and shallow harbors.

questions.question: Are Oceania Allura and Vista sister ships?
questions.answer: Yes. Allura and Vista are sister ships in the Allura Class, sharing the same 1,200-guest capacity, all-veranda stateroom configuration, and contemporary residential design.

questions.question: What is the difference between Oceania Marina and Riviera?
questions.answer: Marina and Riviera are sister ships in the O-Class with almost identical 1,250-guest layouts, culinary facilities, and restaurants. The choice between them generally comes down to your preferred sailing dates and itinerary.

questions.question: Which Oceania ship is best for food lovers?
questions.answer: All Oceania ships place food at the center of the experience, but Marina and Riviera are particularly celebrated for their Culinary Center cooking schools and La Reserve by Wine Spectator pairing dinners. Allura and Vista also offer contemporary concepts like Aquamar Kitchen.

questions.question: Which Oceania ship is best for first-time cruisers?
questions.answer: Allura and Vista are ideal for first-timers seeking contemporary accommodations and all-veranda staterooms. Marina and Riviera are also excellent for travelers wanting an established culinary experience.

questions.question: Are Oceania ships small?
questions.answer: Yes, compared to mainstream mega-ships carrying 4,000–6,000 guests, Oceania's fleet ranges from 670 to 1,250 guests, creating an uncrowded, boutique atmosphere.

questions.question: Do all Oceania ships have veranda staterooms?
questions.answer: Veranda accommodations are available across the entire fleet. Allura and Vista are designed as 100% all-veranda ships, while Marina, Riviera, and R-class ships also offer inside and oceanview staterooms.

questions.question: Which Oceania ship is best for couples?
questions.answer: All seven ships are wonderful for couples. Allura and Vista provide modern romantic luxury, Marina and Riviera offer private dining at Privée, and the smaller R-class ships provide quiet intimacy.

questions.question: Which Oceania ship is best for solo travelers?
questions.answer: Vista and Allura feature dedicated solo concierge veranda staterooms with no single supplement. Across all ships, open-seating dining makes meeting other guests easy and welcoming.

questions.question: Which Oceania ship is best for longer voyages?
questions.answer: Insignia is the traditional flagship for 180-day Around the World Cruises. The upcoming Oceania Aurelia (November 2027) is specifically designed for extended global journeys.

questions.question: Is Oceania Regatta still part of the fleet?
questions.answer: No. Oceania Regatta completed her final voyage for Oceania Cruises in August 2026 and transferred to a new operator. She is no longer sailing under the Oceania brand.

questions.question: What is Oceania Aurelia?
questions.answer: Oceania Aurelia is a future ship debuting in November 2027. She is being created through a major reimagining of Oceania Nautica, featuring approximately 238 spacious suites and 400 crew members for extended world voyages.

questions.question: What is Oceania Sonata?
questions.answer: Oceania Sonata is the first ship in the new Sonata Class, launching in August 2027 with a capacity of approximately 1,390 guests, all-veranda staterooms, and new culinary venues including Nikkei Kitchen.

questions.question: Are Oceania ships good for families?
questions.answer: Oceania is designed for adults, with no kids' clubs, waterslides, or youth programs. Furthermore, Oceania enforces an adults-only policy for new bookings made from January 7, 2026.

questions.question: Do all Oceania ships have the same restaurants?
questions.answer: No. While The Grand Dining Room, Polo Grill, and Toscana are widespread, Jacques is on Marina and Riviera, Tuscan Steak is exclusive to Sirena, and Aquamar Kitchen is on Allura and Vista.

questions.question: How do I choose between Oceania cruise ships?
questions.answer: Start with your desired itinerary and destinations, choose between small-ship intimacy (670 guests) versus mid-size variety (1,200–1,250 guests), compare dining preferences, and consult a luxury cruise advisor.
